name: Programming Fundamentals
description: Writing correct programs from first principles: values and types, control flow, functions, collections, modularity and object-oriented design, with testing and debugging throughout.

topics.name: Values, Types and Expressions
topics.summary: The atoms of a program — what a value is, how types constrain it, and how expressions combine them.

subtopics.name: Primitive Types
subtopics.summary: Integers, floating-point numbers, booleans and characters, and how each is stored.

objectives.text: Name the primitive types of a typical language and state what each can represent
Explain why integer and floating-point arithmetic can give different answers for the same expression
Predict the value and type of a simple expression

subtopics.name: Expressions and Operators
subtopics.summary: Operator precedence, associativity and evaluation order in arithmetic, comparison and logical expressions.

objectives.text: Evaluate an expression by applying precedence and associativity rules in the correct order
Use comparison and logical operators to build a compound condition
Explain short-circuit evaluation and give a case where it changes program behaviour

subtopics.name: Type Conversion and Type Safety
subtopics.summary: Implicit widening, explicit casts, and the errors that follow from losing information.

objectives.text: Distinguish implicit conversion from an explicit cast
Identify where a conversion loses precision or overflows
Explain what static typing catches that dynamic typing does not

topics.name: Control Flow
topics.summary: Choosing between paths and repeating work — the two ways a program departs from straight-line execution.

subtopics.name: Conditionals
subtopics.summary: if, else-if chains and switch, and how to structure a decision without redundant tests.

objectives.text: Write an if/else-if chain that covers every case exactly once
Rewrite nested conditionals into a flatter, equivalent form
Trace which branch executes for given inputs

subtopics.name: Loops and Iteration
subtopics.summary: while, for and do-while loops, loop counters, and the conditions that terminate them.

objectives.text: Choose the appropriate loop form for a counted, sentinel or condition-driven repetition
State a loop's termination condition and argue that it is reached
Identify and fix an off-by-one error in a loop bound

subtopics.name: Nested Iteration and Loop Patterns
subtopics.summary: Nested loops, accumulation, search and early exit — the patterns that recur in every program.

objectives.text: Implement accumulation, search and filter patterns with loops
Use break and continue correctly without obscuring control flow
State how many times the body of a nested loop executes for given bounds

topics.name: Functions and Abstraction
topics.summary: Naming a computation so it can be reused, reasoned about and tested in isolation.

subtopics.name: Defining and Calling Functions
subtopics.summary: Parameters, arguments, return values, and the contract a function promises its caller.

objectives.text: Define a function with parameters and a return value, and call it correctly
State a function's contract as a precondition and a postcondition
Explain the difference between pass-by-value and pass-by-reference

subtopics.name: Scope and Lifetime
subtopics.summary: Where a name is visible, how long its value lives, and why globals cause trouble.

objectives.text: Determine the scope of a variable and which declaration a name resolves to
Distinguish a variable's scope from its lifetime
Explain why shared mutable global state makes a program hard to reason about

subtopics.name: Recursion
subtopics.summary: Functions defined in terms of themselves, with a base case that guarantees termination.

objectives.text: Write a recursive function with a correct base case and a shrinking argument
Trace a recursive call stack and state its depth for a given input
Convert a simple recursion into an equivalent loop

topics.name: Collections
topics.summary: Grouping many values — the built-in structures every program uses before it needs custom ones.

subtopics.name: Arrays and Lists
subtopics.summary: Indexed sequences, fixed versus growable, and the cost of each operation.

objectives.text: Access, insert and remove elements of an indexed sequence
State the cost of indexing, appending and inserting at the front
Explain how a growable array achieves amortised constant-time append

subtopics.name: Maps and Sets
subtopics.summary: Key-value association and membership testing, and when each is the right choice.

objectives.text: Use a map to associate keys with values and a set to test membership
Choose between a list and a map for a lookup-heavy task, with justification
State what makes a value usable as a key

subtopics.name: Strings and Text
subtopics.summary: Text as a sequence of characters, immutability, and the cost of naive concatenation.

objectives.text: Perform indexing, slicing, searching and splitting on strings
Explain why repeated concatenation in a loop can be quadratic
Describe how characters beyond ASCII are encoded

topics.name: Program Structure and Errors
topics.summary: Organising code across files and handling the cases where things go wrong.

subtopics.name: Modules and Namespaces
subtopics.summary: Splitting a program into units with explicit interfaces and controlled visibility.

objectives.text: Split a program into modules with a clear public interface
Explain how namespaces prevent name collisions
Justify hiding an implementation detail behind an interface

subtopics.name: Errors and Exceptions
subtopics.summary: Distinguishing expected failure from a bug, and propagating errors without losing information.

objectives.text: Distinguish a recoverable error from a programming defect
Use exceptions to propagate a failure to a level that can handle it
Explain why silently swallowing an exception is harmful

subtopics.name: Files and Input/Output
subtopics.summary: Reading and writing external data, and why I/O fails in ways computation does not.

objectives.text: Read and write a text file, releasing the resource afterwards
Handle a missing or malformed input file without crashing
Explain why I/O is slow relative to in-memory computation

topics.name: Object-Oriented Foundations
topics.summary: Bundling state with the operations on it — the dominant way large programs are organised.

subtopics.name: Classes and Objects
subtopics.summary: Defining a type with fields and methods, and constructing instances of it.

objectives.text: Define a class with fields, a constructor and methods, and create instances
Distinguish a class from an instance, and instance state from class state
Explain what the receiver (this/self) refers to inside a method

subtopics.name: Encapsulation and Invariants
subtopics.summary: Protecting internal state so an object cannot be put into an invalid configuration.

objectives.text: State a class invariant and show how the constructor establishes it
Use visibility modifiers to prevent external code breaking an invariant
Explain why returning a reference to internal mutable state is dangerous

subtopics.name: Inheritance and Polymorphism
subtopics.summary: Subtypes that can stand in for their supertype, and dispatch chosen at run time.

objectives.text: Define a subclass that overrides a method of its superclass
Explain dynamic dispatch and predict which implementation runs
State the substitution principle and give an example that violates it

topics.name: Correctness and Testing
topics.summary: Establishing that a program does what it claims, and finding out quickly when it does not.

subtopics.name: Unit Testing
subtopics.summary: Writing tests that pin behaviour down, including the boundaries and the empty case.

objectives.text: Write unit tests covering typical, boundary and error cases
Explain why a test suite that only tests the happy path gives false confidence
Choose test inputs that partition the input space

subtopics.name: Debugging
subtopics.summary: Locating a defect by forming and testing hypotheses rather than by guessing.

objectives.text: Reduce a failing case to a minimal reproducible example
Use a debugger or targeted logging to locate the first incorrect state
Distinguish the symptom of a defect from its cause

subtopics.name: Invariants and Assertions
subtopics.summary: Stating what must always be true and checking it where it could fail.

objectives.text: Write an assertion that documents an assumption at a point in the code
Identify a loop invariant for a simple loop
Explain the difference between an assertion and input validation
